{{nihongo|'''Katsuragi Hitokotonushi Shrine'''|葛城一言主神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. It is commonly known as “Ichigon-san” or “Ichikon-ji-san.” The shrine is enshrined facing east on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Yamato Katsuragi|Q11433560|qid=Q11433560|lt=Mount Katsuragi}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines the following two deities<ref name="由緒書">Shrine history pamphlet.</ref>.
* {{ill|Hitokotonushi|Q10864079|qid=Q10864079|lt=Katsuragi no Hitokotonushi Ōkami}} (かつらぎのひとことぬしのおおかみ) – principal deity.
* {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235|lt=Wakatakeru no Mikoto}} (わかたけるのみこと) – the 21st Emperor Yūryaku.

The Meiji-era *Shrine Register* lists the two deities as Kotoshironushi no Mikoto and Wakatakeru no Mikoto, while the *Yamato Shiryō* states that Hitokotonushi is the main deity with Emperor Yūryaku enshrined jointly{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}{{Sfn|奈良県史 5|1989年|pp=449-450}}. In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, the shrine has one seat, and appears as “Katsuki-ni-masu Hitokotonushi Shrine,” indicating that it originally enshrined only {{ill|Hitokotonushi|Q10864079|qid=Q10864079|lt=Hitokotonushi}}{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}. This deity is written as “Hitokotonushi” in the *{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}*, “Hito-kotonushi” in the *{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}*, and “Hito-go-nushi” in the *{{ill|Nihon Ryōiki|Q1606838|qid=Q1606838|lt=Nihon Ryōiki}}*<ref group="原" name="日本霊異記"/>. He is regarded as a god of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=oracles}}, who utters both good and ill fortune in a single word, and is still worshiped today as a deity who grants wishes with a single utterance{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. Although no genealogy is recorded in the *Kojiki* or *Nihon Shoki*, the *{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}*<ref group="原">“Sendai Kuji Hongi,” *Chigi Honki*.</ref> identifies Hitokotonushi as a child of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

[[File:Tennō Yūryaku.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{Center|{{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} and the great boar of {{ill|Mount Yamato Katsuragi|Q11433560|qid=Q11433560|lt=Mount Katsuragi}}}}]]
Regarding Hitokotonushi, a well-known encounter tale with {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} appears in both the *Nihon Shoki*<ref group="原">*Nihon Shoki*, Emperor Yūryaku, 4th year, 2nd month.</ref> and the *Kojiki*<ref group="原">*Kojiki*, section on Emperor Yūryaku.</ref>. According to both accounts, while Emperor Yūryaku was hunting in the mountains of Katsuragi, Hitokotonushi (also written as Hito-kotonushi), who appeared in the same form as the emperor, emerged and competed with him in the hunt{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. In the *Kojiki*, however, the emperor offers a great sword, bow and arrows, and many garments to the deity and worships him, portraying Hitokotonushi as superior, whereas in the *Nihon Shoki* the emperor makes no such offerings and the two are depicted as nearly equal in status{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}. Since the *Kojiki* is considered more archaic, its account is thought to reflect the political circumstances when the {{ill|Katsuragi clan|Q11620908|qid=Q11620908}}—regarded as the clan responsible for the worship of Hitokotonushi—held strong power as imperial in-laws, whereas the *Nihon Shoki* reflects a later period when the Katsuragi clan declined and the status of Hitokotonushi diminished{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}<ref>*Shinpen Nihon Koten Bungaku Zenshū 3: Nihon Shoki (2)*, Shogakukan, 2004 (JapanKnowledge edition), pp. 158–160.</ref>.

In later periods, in Heian-era works such as the *{{ill|Nihon Ryōiki|Q1606838|qid=Q1606838|lt=Nihon Ryōiki}}*<ref group="原" name="日本霊異記">*Nihon Ryōiki*, volume 28.</ref> and the *{{ill|Konjaku Monogatarishū|Q1507085|qid=Q1507085}}*<ref group="原">*Konjaku Monogatari-shū*, volume 11, story 3.</ref>, Hitokotonushi is described as being conscripted by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=En no Gyōja}} (En no Ubasoku / En no Ozunu) to build a bridge between {{ill|Mount Kinpusen|Q10563986|qid=Q10563986}} and Mount Katsuragi, and even bound by a curse after incurring En no Gyōja’s anger—indicating a further decline in divine authority{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}. It is also said that during this forced labor, Hitokotonushi hid the ugliness of his face and worked only at night, not by day; inspired by this tale, {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}} composed a poem in *Oi no Kobumi* (see “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Appearances in works}}”){{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}.

[[File:Tosa-jinja torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tosa Shrine|Q704890|qid=Q704890}} ({{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|Q134093|qid=Q134093}}{{ill|Kōchi, Kōchi|Q200251|qid=Q200251}})}}{{small|Currently enshrines {{ill|Hitokotonushi|Q10864079|qid=Q10864079|lt=Hitokotonushi}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ajisukitakahikone no Kami}}.}}]]
According to the *{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ar|شوكو نيهونغي|ca|Shoku Nihongi|cs|Šoku Nihongi|de|Shoku Nihongi|es|Shoku Nihongi|eu|Shoku Nihongi|fa|شوکو نیهونگی|ff|Shoku Nihongi|fr|Shoku Nihongi|id|Shoku Nihongi|it|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|ko|속일본기|ms|Shoku Nihongi|pt|Shoku Nihongi|ru|Сёку нихонги|simple|Shoku Nihongi|sl|Šoku Nihongi|th|โชกุนิฮงงิ|tr|Shoku Nihongi|uk|Сьоку Ніхонґі|zh|續日本紀|qid=Q611399}}*, entry for the 8th year of {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}} ({{ill|764|Q31163|qid=Q31163}})<ref group="原">*Shoku Nihongi*, Tenpyō-hōji 8 (764), 11th month, day 7.</ref>, a deity called “Takakamo no Kami,” who had competed in hunting with Emperor Yūryaku, had been exiled to {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}}, but in that year was re-enshrined in his original place{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. However, one passage cited in the *{{ill|Shaku Nihongi|Q2710483|qid=Q2710483}}* from the *Rekiryoku* states that in Tenpyō-hōji 8, Hitokotonushi was brought back from Tosa and enshrined in Katsuragi{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}. Another excerpt from the *Tosa Province Fudoki* cited in the *Shaku Nihongi* notes that the deity of Takakamo Taisha in Tosa (present-day {{ill|Tosa Shrine|Q704890|qid=Q704890}}) is Hitokotonushi no Mikoto, though another tradition identifies him as {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|Q506610|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto}}. Thus, the sources show confusion between Hitokotonushi and Takakamo no Kami (Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, enshrined at {{ill|Takakamo Shrine|Q11673295|qid=Q11673295}}){{Sfn|平林章仁|2013年|pp=235-253}}. Additionally, due to similarities in name and their nature as oracle deities, some theories identify Hitokotonushi with {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto}}{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. Shrine tradition holds that the current site is where Hitokotonushi manifested<ref name="由緒書"/>.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=official histories}}, it is recorded that in the 3rd year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}})<ref group="原" name="嘉祥3年"/>, the divine rank of “Katsuki Hitokotonushi no Kami” was raised to Senior Third Rank, and that in the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten’an}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) in the first month<ref group="原" name="貞観元年正月"/>, it was promoted to Junior Second Rank, Second Class of Merit{{Sfn|葛城坐一言主神社（式内社）|1982年}}. In September of the same year, the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} (859)<ref group="原">*Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku*, Jōgan 1 (859), 9th month, 8th day (see {{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}).</ref>, envoys were dispatched to present offerings to Hitokotonushi and other deities in prayer for rain and wind{{Sfn|葛城坐一言主神社（式内社）|1982年}}. In the 5th year of {{ill|Shōryaku|de|Shōryaku|fa|شوریاکو|fr|Ère Shōryaku|ia|Shoryaku|id|Shōryaku|ja|正暦|ko|쇼랴쿠|ru|Сёряку|simple|Shōryaku|sr|Шорјаку|tr|Shōryaku|uk|Сьоряку|zh|正曆 (日本)|zh_yue|正曆 (日本)|qid=Q1324858}} ({{ill|994|ab|994|af|994|am|994 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|994|ar|994|ary|994|arz|994|ast|994|avk|994|az|994|azb|۹۹۴ (میلادی)|bar|994|bcl|994|be|994|be_x_old|994|bg|994|bn|৯৯৪|bpy|মারি ৯৯৪|br|994|bs|994.|ca|994|cdo|994 nièng|ceb|994|ckb|٩٩٤|crh|994|cs|994|csb|994|cv|994|cy|994|da|994|de|994|el|994|eml|994|eo|994|es|994|et|994|eu|994|fa|۹۹۴ (میلادی)|fi|994|fo|994|fr|994|fy|994|ga|994|gan|994年|gd|994|gl|994|he|994|hi|994|ht|994 (almanak jilyen)|hu|994|hy|994|id|994|ilo|994|io|994|is|994|it|994|ja|994年|jv|994|ka|994|kaa|994|kk|994 жыл|ko|994년|la|994|lb|994|lij|994|lmo|994|lt|994 m.|lv|994. gads|map_bms|994|mdf|994|mg|994|mhr|994|mi|994|mk|994|mr|इ.स. ९९४|mrj|994 и|ms|994|mzn|۹۹۴|nah|994|nap|994|nds|994|new|सन् ९९४|nl|994|nn|994|no|994|nrm|994|nso|994|oc|994|or|୯୯୪|os|994-æм аз|pl|994|pnb|994|pt|994|qu|994|ro|994|ru|994 год|rue|994|sa|९९४|scn|994|sd|994ع|se|994|sh|994.|shn|994|si|994|simple|994|sk|994|sl|994|smn|994|sq|994|sr|994|su|994|sv|994|sw|994|tg|Соли 994|th|พ.ศ. 1537|tk|994|tl|994|tly|994|tr|994|tt|994 ел|uk|994|ur|994ء|uz|994|vec|994|vi|994|war|994|wuu|994年|xmf|994|zh|994年|zh_min_nan|994 nî|zh_yue|994年|qid=Q24114}}), fourth month<ref group="原">*Honchō Seiki*, Shōryaku 5 (994), 4th month.</ref>, offerings were again presented, with members of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|el|Αδελφότητα Νακατόμι|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447}} serving as envoys, in response to epidemics and fires{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, compiled in the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274}} ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed in Yamato Province, {{ill|Katsujō district|Q11620858|qid=Q11620858}}, as “Katsuki-ni-masu Hitokotonushi Shrine, Myōjin Taisha, Monthly and New Harvest Offerings,” indicating its status as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Myōjin Taisha}} and that it received offerings from the court at the {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|葛城坐一言主神社（式内社）|1982年}}.

Subsequent history is unclear. In the past, there was a temple called Ichigon-ji to the southeast of the shrine as a {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}}, but it has since been abandoned{{Sfn|一言主神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and in March {{ill|1883|ab|1883|af|1883|als|1883|am|1883 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1883|ar|1883|ary|1883|arz|1883|ast|1883|av|1883 === Festivals ===
List of annual festivals held at Katsuragi Hitokotonushi Shrine<ref name="由緒書"/>.
* New Year’s Day Festival (January 1)
* Setsubun Festival (around February 3)
* Spring Grand Festival (April 5)
* Inari Shrine Festival (May 3)
* Summer Purification Festival (June 30)
* Autumn Grand Festival (Sacred Fire Festival) (September 15)
* Zako Festival (second Sunday of October)
* Ichiyō Raifuku Festival (winter solstice)

=== Appearances in works ===
* {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}} *Oi no Kobumi*{{Sfn|葛木坐一言主神社（神々）|1985年}}
*: {{Cquote|{{small|As I made a pilgrimage through the land of Yamato and passed the foot of Mount Katsuragi, flowers were in full bloom on all sides, the peaks veiled in haze—at dawn the scenery was all the more alluring. Hearing people speak ill of the appearance of that god,}}<br /> Still I longed to see—through flowers, the dawning face of the god|20px||*Oi no Kobumi*}}
